extracted.intended_audience: gene therapy researchers, preclinical immunologists, and NIH grant reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Design and evaluation of preclinical experiments to measure AAV capsid antigen presentation, transduction efficiency, and immune evasion in vitro and in multiple mouse models (including humanized liver xenografts), testing capsid mutants and proteasome inhibitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dose-response of capsid antigen presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine how varying vector dose affects AAV capsid antigen presentation and transgene expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer different particle doses (examples given: 10^8, 10^9, 10^10, 10^11, 2x10^11, 10^12) into mice and measure antigen presentation and transgene expression; use 5 mice per group typical. For in vivo dose-response, infuse OT-1 spleen cells 3 days after AAV injection to analyze CD8 T cell proliferation. Evaluate both antigen presentation efficiency and kinetics across doses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinetics of antigen presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the time-course of capsid antigen presentation after AAV administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze capsid-specific T cell proliferation and antigen presentation at multiple time points (explicitly: day 3, 21, 41, 61). Expect stronger presentation early after administration with gradual decrease; determine kinetics in HepG2 in vitro and in various mouse strains in vivo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of empty versus full AAV particles on cross-presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess how empty capsids (empty particles) influence capsid antigen cross-presentation from full-particle transduction and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use groups with varying amounts of empty or full particles (example groups: 0, 1x10^10, 3x10^10,1x10^11, 3x10^11, 1x10^12 spiked with 1x10^11 full or empty particles). Measure transgene expression (5 mice x 6 groups = 30) and antigen presentation (e.g., 5 mice/group x 6 groups x 4 time points = 120). Include control/no treatment groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of capsid mutants to enhance liver transduction and modulate antigen presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate AAV capsid mutants (e.g., AAV2G9, AAV2D, AAV2 Y-F, AAV2 K532R, AAV8 Y-F, AAV8 K137R, AAV2-MT4, AAV8-MT2) for increased transduction and altered capsid antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize mutants in vitro and in vivo for transgene expression (luciferase, GFP) and capsid antigen presentation (OT-1 proliferation, HepG2/H2kb assay). Example: inject 1x10^11 particles IV and compare transduction and antigen presentation vs wtAAV. For transgene expression groups: 5 mice/group x 19 viruses used in proposal = 95 mice. Determine dose-response and kinetics for mutants as for wt vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of proteasome inhibitors on transduction and antigen presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine how proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib, carfilzomib) at different concentrations/doses affect AAV transduction and capsid antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study in vitro dose ranges (examples: concentrations in nM such as 10 nM, 100 nM, 1 uM) and in vivo doses (example: 10 µg, 100 µg, 1 mg, 10 mg/kg). Note observed biphasic effects: high doses (in vitro) can inhibit antigen presentation while increasing transduction; low doses (10 nM) may increase antigen presentation without increasing transgene expression; intermediate doses may increase both. Monitor transgene expression by luciferase imaging and antigen presentation assays; monitor toxicities (body weight, blood chemistry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of capsid mutants with proteasome inhibitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether combining multi-modified AAV mutants with proteasome inhibitors further enhances liver transduction and reduces capsid antigen presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administer AAV2-MT4 or AAV8-MT2 mutants together with proteasome inhibitors and compare transgene expression and antigen presentation to single mutants or inhibitor alone. Examine multiple vector doses (examples: 10^8–10^11) in presence/absence of inhibitors. Anticipate higher transgene expression and lower or undetectable antigen presentation, but include alternative plans if combination does not perform as expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of capsid ubiquitination via residue mutation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rationally mutate capsid residues (tyrosine→phenylalanine Y→F, lysine→arginine K→R, or S/T→A) to reduce ubiquitination and proteasome-mediated degradation, aiming to lower antigen presentation and boost transduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include AAV2 Y-F triple mutant (Y730+500+444F), AAV2 K532R, AAV8 K137R. Evaluate ubiquitination levels and transduction in vitro and in vivo. Use ubiquitin conjugation assays and immunoblotting to confirm reduced ubiquitination. Consider that some mutations raise transduction but may still permit capsid antigen presentation over time; further testing required.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vitro antigen presentation assays using OVA SIINFEKL substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use OVA SIINFEKL peptide inserted into the HI loop of capsids to measure capsid antigen cross-presentation in cell lines (e.g., HepG2/H2kb) via OT-1 T cell readouts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clone SIINFEKL into HI loop of various capsid mutants (pXR2G9-OVA, pXR2D-OVA, etc.). Infect HepG2/H2kb cells, co-culture with OT-1 T cells or measure T cell proliferation/activation. Use luciferase or GFP reporters to monitor transduction. Expect that HI loop swapping will not markedly change infectivity/tropism based on prior data but include alternative CTL generation if OVA insertion impairs transduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo antigen presentation assay using OT-1 adoptive transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure capsid antigen presentation in mice by adoptive transfer of OT-1 spleen cells and assessment of CD8 T cell proliferation after AAV-OVA administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical protocol: administer AAV-OVA vectors IV, at specified dose (e.g., 1x10^11 particles), and 3 days after AAV injection infuse OT-1 spleen cells; analyze capsid-specific T cell proliferation at chosen time points (day 3, 21, 41, 61). Use appropriate mouse strains (C57BL) and include proper controls. For dose-response studies, vary vector doses and monitor proliferation accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and characterization of human liver-tropic mutants via humanized mouse directed evolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Use DNA shuffling and in vivo selection in human liver xenografted mice (FRG mice) to isolate AAV capsid variants with human hepatocyte tropism and immune-evasion capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct shuffled capsid libraries from 12 serotypes and selected mutants (including lysine/S/T modifications), inject library IV with Ad5 helper, perform iterative recovery cycles (harvest liver, extract Hirt DNA, re-inject pooled supernatant for 3–4 cycles), amplify recovered capsid sequences, package best candidates encoding GFP, and test in xenografted mice. Use cell sorting for human HLA-ABC+/GFP+ hepatocytes to isolate human-tropic variants. Include structural and sequence analysis of recovered mutants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and justification of mouse strains and humanized models
rubrics_metrics.description: Select appropriate mouse strains for each experimental question (e.g., C57BL for baseline, TAP-/- and Cat S-/- to probe antigen processing pathways, OT-1 for OVA-specific readouts, FRG humanized mice for human hepatocyte tropism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider known biology (e.g., TAP-/- mice may have lower overall MHC class expression but still can show strong antigen presentation). Use FRG mice for robust human liver repopulation; follow established engraftment protocols and measure human albumin to assess repopulation. Tailor strain selection to assay sensitivity and biological question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of in vitro ubiquitination assays and immunoblotting to detect capsid ubiquitination
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess capsid ubiquitination by performing ubiquitin–protein conjugation assays and detecting ubiquitinated capsid proteins via immunoblot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol outline: mix conjugation fractions with heat-denatured AAV particles, incubate at 37°C for 4 hr, resolve SDS-denatured samples on gradient gels, immunoblot with mouse anti-ubiquitin (P4D1) and anti-AAV clone B1 for VP1/VP2/VP3. In cell-based detection, immunoprecipitate capsid with anti-AAV (B1), blot with anti-ubiquitin after MG132 or mock treatment. Visualize with enhanced chemiluminescence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural and sequence analysis of recovered mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize candidate capsid mutants structurally and by sequence alignment to map modified domains and conserved regions that influence tropism and immune recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use molecular modeling tools (Pymol, SWISS-MODEL), available VP3 PDB templates, Vector NTI for sequence alignment, and viperdb for mapping two-fold/three-fold/five-fold axes. Generate 3D ribbon models of dimers/trimers/pentamers to map domain locations on capsid surface and inform rational design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring toxicity and animal health parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Track clinical and laboratory measures of toxicity when administering AAV vectors and proteasome inhibitors in vivo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor body weight and blood chemistry (through institutional animal clinical chemistry core). Use IACUC-approved protocols and Just-in-time submission. Consider toxicities of high-dose proteasome inhibitors when interpreting antigen presentation results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and experimental group design conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan animal numbers and group sizes adequate for readouts of transduction and antigen presentation, typically using 5 mice per experimental group and defined numbers of OT-1 mice for adoptive transfer assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: 5 mice/group for transgene expression assays; detailed mouse counts per aim are enumerated (e.g., Aim 1 total = 720 mice across subexperiments; Aim 2.1 transgene expression: 95 C57BL mice for 19 viruses). Use these conventions to ensure statistical power and replicate numbers in endpoint assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated outcomes, potential pitfalls, and alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate expected results and contingency plans if experiments do not behave as predicted (e.g., OVA insertion alters tropism, low virus recovery from xenografts, mutants not improving transduction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of alternatives: generate CTLs against wild-type capsid (Ad vector delivery, peptide-pulsed DC immunization, direct peptide immunization) if OVA substitution impairs transduction; amplify recovered genomes in 293 cells with helper plasmids if yields from xenograft are too low; construct shuffled libraries without further residue substitution and then modify recovered mutants post-selection. Explicitly note that many outcomes are possible and describe fallback strategies.
